question.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the norm of the vector $x$ in terms of $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖x‖ & =\sqrt{{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}+{x}_{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+(3k)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+9{k}^{2}+4+9} \\  & =\sqrt{9{k}^{2}+14}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given equation  $‖x‖=5\sqrt{2},$ we obtain an equation that we can solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{9{k}^{2}+14} & =5\sqrt{2} \\ {(\sqrt{9{k}^{2}+14})}^{2} & ={(5\sqrt{2})}^{2} \\ 9{k}^{2}+14 & =25\cdot 2 \\ 9{k}^{2}+14 & =50 \\ 9{k}^{2} & =36 \\ {k}^{2} & =4 \\ k & =\pm 2.\end{aligned}
$$
